subject.title: fix(sessions): sweep orphan store temp files

question: Should automatic stale session-store temp cleanup run inside `loadSessionStore`, or should it stay in a bounded startup/cleanup owner path that reuses the existing disk-budget cleanup primitive?
rationale: Both choices can fix the disk leak, but the current PR changes the read-path deletion boundary and could affect startup/read latency on large session directories, which needs owner intent rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Move Cleanup Out Of Reads
options.body: Route the automatic sweep through a bounded startup or explicit cleanup path and reuse `pruneUnreferencedSessionArtifacts` / `isSessionStoreTempArtifactName` so ordinary store reads remain side-effect-light.

options.title: Accept Load-Time Deletion
options.body: Allow `loadSessionStore` to reclaim stale temp files during cold and `skipCache` reads, but require rebase, conflict resolution, and performance proof on a large sessions directory before merge.

options.title: Pause This PR
options.body: Hold or close this branch if maintainers decide current cleanup and `openclaw sessions cleanup` are sufficient until a broader session-store maintenance design lands.

recommendation.title: Move Cleanup Out Of Reads
recommendation.body: Route the automatic sweep through a bounded startup or explicit cleanup path and reuse `pruneUnreferencedSessionArtifacts` / `isSessionStoreTempArtifactName` so ordinary store reads remain side-effect-light.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely to decide the session-storage owner boundary because recent history shows adjacent session metadata, cleanup documentation, and refactor work across these files.
